cover.headline: The world's off-highway tyre specialist, betting its balance sheet on new markets; fairly priced after the Q1 rally
cover.lead: Balkrishna Industries (BKT) makes off-highway tyres (OHT) for tractors, harvesters, mining trucks, loaders and industrial machines, ~64% of them exported (Europe 40%, Americas 13% of FY26 volume), from four Indian plants with captive carbon black. FY26 EPS fell 25% to ₹64.3 on currency-hedge losses and a 50% US duty; Q1FY27 bounced (volume +16%, profit +57%). We forecast EPS of ₹73.8 / ₹87.8 / ₹107.0 for FY27-29E, below the street's FY28E range (₹94-105). The street values BKT on **P/E on one-year-forward EPS** (22-28x FY28E). Applying the house rule (its forward P/E median since 2021, 31.2x, cut by the 20.6% tyre-sector de-rating) gives **25x Sep-28E EPS of ₹97.4 = {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): we initiate with HOLD**, just short of the BUY threshold. Cross-checks: EV/EBITDA ₹1,969, DCF ₹1,665, both below the price. Bull case {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear case {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.h: The core is a real niche, and FY27 is a recovery year
arguments.p: BKT has ~5-6% of the global OHT market with 3,600+ sizes, Indian costs and its own carbon black and power at Bhuj; its EBITDA margin (18-31% over FY16-26) is far above Indian tyre peers (12-16% in FY26). Q1FY27 brought record volume (93,770 MT, +16%), India up to ~40% of volume, the US reopening at a ~10% duty, and hedges rolling to ~₹107/EUR from ₹94-99. We model FY27E revenue +23% and EPS +15%.

arguments.h: But margins are hostage to things BKT does not control
arguments.p: FY26 showed it: a ₹517 cr swing in currency gains and losses (standalone) and a US duty of 50% cut EPS by a quarter while volume rose 1%. In FY27 raw materials are up again (crude, Middle East freight): management expects ~2pp of margin to go in Q2. We assume {{F.ebitdaMargin.0|pct}} for FY27E and {{F.ebitdaMargin.2|pct}} by FY29E, below management's 23-25% "endeavour" and the street's bulls.

arguments.h: The new businesses are a bet, not a moat
arguments.p: ₹6,800 cr of capex to FY29 (two-thirds of net worth) goes largely into carbon black for third parties, truck and bus radials, two-wheeler and passenger-car tyres in India, crowded markets with entrenched leaders. Debt has risen to ₹4,690 cr (Jun-26) and ROCE fell to 11%. We assume on-highway revenue of ₹1,100 cr by FY29E, well short of the ₹5,000 cr 2030 target.

At ₹2,117 BKT trades at 24.1x our FY28E and 21.7x Sep-28E EPS. Its own forward P/E has a median of 31.2x since 2021, but Indian tyre stocks sat 20.6% below their five-year medians on 30-Sep-2026. That gives 25x and {{dcf.tp|inr}}. Our EPS, not the multiple, is why we sit below the post-Q1 street median (₹2,525): at the street's 27x we would be at ~₹2,630.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): the size of the raw-material hit (management: ~2pp of margin) against the full ~5% price increase and the better euro hedges.
US trade: whether the ~10% duty holds and whether the reciprocal-tariff refunds BKT has filed for (as importer of record) are paid; US back to 15-16% of revenue is management's aim.
The European farm season (heat waves, farm incomes) and dealer inventories, which drive ~40% of volume.
On-highway ramp-up: TBR and two-wheeler sales from Q2, the passenger-car pilot in Q3FY27; the first disclosure of on-highway revenue.
Capex peaking in FY27 (₹2,500-3,000 cr) and free cash flow turning positive in FY28E; dividend policy once capex falls.

sections.title: A specialist in off-highway tyres, sold mostly abroad and mostly as replacements

blocks.p: Balkrishna Industries sells tyres under the BKT brand for machines that work off the road: **agricultural** tyres for tractors, harvesters, sprayers and trailers (58.8% of FY26 volume) and **OTR** tyres for construction, mining, ports and industrial machines (37.5%), plus ATV, gardening and other tyres (3.7%). It makes 3,600+ sizes in four tyre plants (Waluj in Maharashtra, Bhiwadi and Chopanki in Rajasthan, Bhuj in Gujarat) with ~360,000 MTPA of achievable output, and sells in 160 countries. 70.1% of volume goes to the replacement market (farmers, contractors and mines buying through distributors) and 28.7% to equipment makers. By destination, FY26 volume was Europe 40%, India 36.3%, the Americas 13.2% and the rest of the world 10.5%; exports were ~64% of revenue.

Two newer businesses sit beside the tyres. **Carbon black**: BKT makes its own at Bhuj (360,000 MTPA since Q1FY27, with 64 MW of captive power from the process gases) and sells the surplus to other tyre and plastics makers: ~9% of FY26 revenue and ~10% of Q1FY27. **On-highway tyres** for India: truck and bus radials (from Feb/Apr-2026), two-wheeler tyres and, from a pilot in Q3FY27, passenger-car radials. Management targets ₹23,000 cr of revenue by FY30 (OHT 70%, carbon black 10%, on-highway 20%). BKT reports all of this as one segment and does not disclose revenue by business in rupees.

sections.title: Forty years of building a niche; the last five spent on capacity and new markets

blocks.p: BKT was built by the Poddar family from a single plant at Aurangabad (1987) into the largest Indian maker of off-highway tyres, mostly by exporting radial farm tyres to European dealers at prices below the global majors. The Bhuj greenfield site (from 2015) brought captive carbon black (2020) and power. The post-Covid boom lifted revenue 43% in FY22; the freight and raw-material spike cut the margin to 18% in FY23. Since 2024 the company has widened its ambitions: advanced carbon materials, a ₹6,800 cr capex plan and entry into Indian on-highway tyres. There have been no acquisitions, demergers or share issues in the last five years: 19.33 cr shares of ₹2 each, unchanged in FY25 and FY26 (AR FY26 note 17).

sections.title: A slow-growing global market (~3% a year); India and mining are the bright spots

blocks.p: Off-highway tyres are a small, specialised part of the tyre market. Smithers (quoted in BKT's FY26 annual report) expects global OHT volume to grow from 52.5 mn units in 2026 to 57 mn in 2029, under 3% a year. Demand follows farm incomes and equipment sales in Europe and North America, construction and mining activity, and dealer inventories, which swung hard in FY23-25. The global majors (Michelin, Bridgestone, Yokohama's off-highway business and others) dominate the first-fit market for large equipment makers; BKT's edge is the replacement market, where farmers trade down from the premium brands. India's OHT market is small (~USD 1.22 bn) but growing ~5.52% a year on farm mechanisation and infrastructure; BKT already has 18-19% of it.

bullets: **Headwinds in 2025-26.** Lower farm incomes and high dealer inventories in Europe and North America (AR FY26); US import duty on India raised to 50% mid-Q2FY26, ~10% by May-2026; Middle East conflict raising crude-linked raw materials, freight and container costs (Q4FY26 and Q1FY27 calls).

**Raw materials.** Natural and synthetic rubber, carbon black feedstock, nylon and steel cord: crude-linked items rose again in Q4FY26-Q2FY27 (management: +4-5% in Q4FY26, +7-8% in Q1FY27, +5% more over Q2-Q3).
**Freight.** Container and vessel availability and freight (4.5-7% of revenue in FY26-27) hit an exporter shipping heavy tyres to Europe and the Americas.
**Carbon black.** A ~15.2 mn tonne global market growing ~2.3% a year by volume (to ~17 mn t by 2030); India ~USD 1.8-1.9 bn, growing 4-5% (AR FY26).
**On-highway tyres in India.** A large market led by MRF, Apollo, CEAT and JK, all adding capacity; BKT enters truck radials, two-wheelers and premium passenger-car tyres as a newcomer.

blocks.callout: **Verdict:** the tailwinds that reach BKT most directly are Indian, and India is the lower-margin market. The global OHT market grows ~3% a year, so BKT's growth outside India has to come from share gains in Europe and the US. FY27 looks good because the base is weak (tariffs, hedging losses), not because the market has turned into a growth market.

sections.title: OHT: volume flat for two years, then a record Q1; price and the euro do the rest

blocks.p: BKT sold 2,92,600 MT of OHT tyres in FY24, 3,15,273 MT in FY25 (+8%) and 3,17,356 MT in FY26 (+1%). FY26 had two halves: the US duty on Indian goods went to 50% in the middle of Q2 and BKT stopped shipping to the US (Q2 volume 70,252 MT, −4%), then Europe recovered as dealer stocks cleared and Q4 set a record. Q1FY27 beat it: 93,770 MT (+16%), with India ~40% of volume, Europe stable on a weak base and the US better at a ~10% duty. Revenue per tonne rose ~3% in FY26 (₹341k vs ₹330k, standalone, before FX) and ~7% in Q1FY27 (₹367k vs ₹342k), on price increases (3-5% by May, ~5% more in Q1) and the euro.

blocks.p: **Currency is the biggest swing factor.** About 64% of revenue is exported and BKT sells euros and dollars forward. At Mar-2026 it had sold EUR 259 mn against the rupee for FY27 at ₹107.16, EUR 238 mn against the dollar and USD 163 mn against the rupee (plus EUR 73 mn of other contracts). When the rupee falls below the hedged rates, as it did in FY26, the gap shows up as realised losses in revenue (₹164 cr) and mark-to-market losses below EBITDA (₹144 cr), and a ₹575 cr loss on hedges went through other comprehensive income. In FY27 the hedge rate is higher, so the realised loss shrank to ₹36 cr in Q1 and unrealised turned into a ₹57 cr gain.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** we model OHT volume +11% in FY27E (Q1 +16% on a weak base; Q3-Q4 against records), then +8% and +7% as capacity moves towards 425,000 MTPA, and price/mix of +7.2% in FY27E (price increases and euro hedges, less India mix), then ~3% a year. That is OHT revenue of ₹11,720 cr in FY27E. MOSL and Anand Rathi model 12-13% volume CAGR for FY26-28E; we are a little lower (9.5%), because the global market grows ~3% and Q1 included a rebound.

sections.title: Carbon black and on-highway tyres: a third of the 2030 plan, with no track record yet

blocks.p: **Carbon black.** BKT built carbon black at Bhuj to secure its own supply and power; with phase 2 (Q1FY27, ₹800 cr) capacity is 360,000 MTPA, well above its own needs. Management said ~70% of the new capacity's output is sold outside and ~30% used inside, at "industry average" margins. Third-party sales were ~9% of FY26 revenue (~₹974 cr) and ~10% in Q1FY27. We grow it 38% / 12% / 10% (₹1,656 cr by FY29E). The plan for 2030 is ~10% of ₹23,000 cr. This is a commodity business, priced off crude-linked feedstock; it helps BKT's costs more than its margin.

**On-highway tyres.** BKT launched truck and bus radials (Feb/Apr-2026, phase 1 of the CV radial project: ₹750 cr, 800 tyres a day, fungible with OHT), re-launched two-wheeler tyres and plans a passenger-car radial pilot in Q3FY27, all for the Indian replacement market, through ~90 distributors appointed for the purpose. Management calls FY27 "a year of building the portfolio" and FY28 "serious business", and keeps a ₹5,000 cr revenue target for 2030; it will not disclose on-highway revenue yet. We assume ₹200 / 600 / 1,100 cr for FY27-29E (Anand Rathi: ₹600 cr in FY28E at mid-single-digit margins) and start-up losses inside our FY27E margin.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** OHT is a niche BKT dominates on cost; Indian on-highway tyres are a scale business where MRF, Apollo, CEAT and JK have brands, dealers and OEM relationships. BKT's plan to win through "a great product strategy" and premium positioning is plausible in two-wheelers and premium SUV tyres, but it will take years and dilute margins and returns meanwhile. We give it little value: our FY29E on-highway revenue is a fifth of the 2030 target.

blocks.callout: **Honest verdict:** BKT has a genuine but narrow moat: the widest OHT range from a low-cost base, sold mainly in replacement markets where buyers trade down from Michelin and Bridgestone. That has earned an EBITDA margin of 18-31% over a decade. It does not protect against the farm cycle, freight, the rupee or US trade policy, and it does not extend to Indian on-highway tyres or merchant carbon black, where BKT is a newcomer with no cost or brand edge.

sections.title: Revenue tripled in ten years; profit has not grown since FY21

blocks.p: BKT's revenue was ₹3,237 cr in FY16 and ₹10,823 cr in FY26: 12.8% a year. Most of that came in one jump: the post-Covid farm and construction boom lifted revenue 43% in FY22. Since then growth has been slow (6.9% a year FY22-26) and profit has gone sideways: EPS was ₹60.9 in FY21 and ₹64.3 in FY26. Three things explain it. The EBITDA margin fell from 31% (FY21) to 18% (FY23) on freight and raw materials and has not gone back above 24%; depreciation and interest grew with a ₹6,800 cr capex plan; and in FY26 currency turned against BKT. The rupee fell below the rates at which BKT had sold its euros and dollars forward, and a US import duty of 50% (from mid-Q2FY26) stopped its US shipments. FY26 EPS fell 25% to ₹64.3.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** BKT is still one of the most profitable tyre makers in the world for its size, but the last five years show the limits of the model. Its margin depends on three things it does not control: farm and mining cycles in Europe and the Americas, freight and crude-linked raw materials, and the rupee against its hedge book. FY26 was a currency year as much as a business year: standalone FX moved from a ₹209 cr gain (FY25) to a ₹308 cr loss, a ₹517 cr swing, more than the ₹406 cr fall in standalone profit. That swing partly reverses in FY27 only because the hedges now sit at higher rates.

blocks.callout: **Why it matters:** the Q1 profit jump is mostly the base: Q1FY26 carried a ₹154 cr unrealised FX loss (standalone) that turned into a ₹57 cr gain. The operating margin fell ~3pp (standalone) on raw materials, India mix and higher staff costs, and management expects ~2pp more pressure in Q2. Our FY27E EBITDA margin of {{F.ebitdaMargin.0|pct}} assumes ~19.5-20% in Q2-Q3 and ~21% in Q4.

sections.title: A ₹6,800 cr build-out has turned BKT from net cash to net debt and ROCE to 11%

blocks.p: BKT funds growth itself. Over FY21-26 it generated ₹9,790 cr of operating cash, spent ₹9,868 cr on capex and paid ₹2,029 cr of dividends; borrowings rose from ₹1,001 cr to ₹4,111 cr. The current plan is the largest in its history: ₹6,800 cr to FY29 for carbon black (now 360,000 MTPA), captive power, CV radial and passenger-car tyres, more OHT capacity (to 425,000 MTPA) and automation. ₹2,984 cr went out in FY26 and ~₹1,000 cr in Q1FY27, with ₹1,500-2,000 cr more due in FY27. ROCE fell from 24% (FY21-22) to 11% (FY26) on Screener's basis, because capital employed rose faster than profit and CWIP reached ₹2,472 cr.

Management says ROCE will not fall significantly once the projects run fully; on our numbers ROE recovers only to ~14-15% by FY29E, below the 15-22% of FY22-25.

sections.title: Earnings quality: real cash and a clean balance sheet, but currency and treasury gains move profit a lot

bullets: **Cash conversion is good.** Cash from operations was 107% of net profit in FY25 and 181% in FY26 (₹2,249 cr), helped by depreciation (₹775 cr) and lower working capital. Free cash flow was negative in FY26 (capex ₹3,003 cr) and will be again in FY27E.

**Currency moves the P&L in three places.** Realised hedge gains or losses sit in revenue, unrealised ones in other expenses (consolidated) or below EBITDA (standalone), and in FY25 a ₹267 cr FX gain sat in other income. Between FY25 and FY26 the standalone swing was ₹517 cr; a further ₹575 cr hedge loss went through OCI. Reported margins and EPS are therefore not comparable year to year.

**Half of other income is market-linked treasury gains.** FY26 other income of ₹252 cr included ₹80 cr of mark-to-market gains and ₹52 cr of realised gains on investments; Screener tags ₹171 cr of such items as "exceptional". They recur while BKT holds a ~₹2,552 cr market-linked book (8.1% total return in FY26), but they fall as the book is run down for capex. We forecast ₹{{F.otherIncome.0|num}} cr in FY27E and ₹{{F.otherIncome.1|num}} cr in FY28E (twelve months to Jun-26: ₹244 cr).

**Non-core investments.** ₹636 cr in strategic equity (₹593 cr NSE stake, start-up preference shares) and ₹424 cr in AIFs and real-estate debt funds. Small against net worth, but not what an industrial company needs, and the NSE stake's value is not cash.

**CWIP is large.** ₹2,472 cr at Mar-26 (Screener), up from ₹986 cr: carbon black, CV radial and PCR projects. Our model depreciates new capex at once and holds CWIP flat, which slightly overstates FY27E depreciation timing.

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: AMBER.** Clean audit, real cash, no related-party oddities found. The amber is for the hedging: large, volatile FX gains and losses spread across revenue, expenses, other income and OCI, which make the margin hard to read, plus market-linked treasury gains in other income. A second auditor (Deloitte, proposed May-2026) is a positive.

sections.title: Net debt of ₹922 cr at Mar-26 and ₹1,725 cr at Jun-26: modest, but rising

blocks.p: At Mar-2026 BKT had ₹4,111 cr of borrowings, mostly short-term export credit (₹3,218 cr) plus ₹750 cr of NCDs at 7.20-7.55% (2029-31) and term loans, against ₹3,124 cr of investments and ₹65 cr of cash. ₹637 cr of the investments is strategic equity (₹593 cr in NSE shares, start-ups) and ₹424 cr is in alternative and real-estate funds, so the liquid treasury is ~₹2,000-2,500 cr. On the company's basis net debt was ₹895 cr at Mar-26 and ₹1,725 cr at Jun-26 (standalone). Working capital is heavy for an exporter: ~126 days of inventory, ~49 of receivables and ~64 of payables in FY26. The balance sheet also carries the hedge book: a ₹575 cr loss on cash-flow hedges went through other comprehensive income in FY26.

sections.title: Our honest summary: a good niche business at a fair price; HOLD, on the edge of BUY

blocks.callout: **What you are buying:** the world's leading specialist in replacement off-highway tyres outside the global majors, with ~5-6% of the global market, Indian costs, its own carbon black and power, and an 18-31% EBITDA margin over a decade. It is recovering from a currency-and-tariff year (FY26 EPS −25%) with record volumes, and spending ₹6,800 cr to enter carbon black and Indian on-highway tyres, which takes it from net cash to ~₹2,000 cr of net debt at the peak.

**What you are paying:** 28.7x our FY27E and 24.1x FY28E EPS. BKT's own forward P/E has a median of 31.2x since 2021; Indian tyre stocks were 20.6% below their five-year medians on 30-Sep-2026, which gives 25x Sep-28E EPS and {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}). That is HOLD on our rule, just short of the +15% BUY line; the EV/EBITDA and DCF cross-checks (₹1,969 and ₹1,665) are below the price, so we do not stretch for a BUY.

**This is mainly an earnings call.** Our multiple (25x) is close to the street's range (22-28x); our FY28E EPS (₹87.8) is 6-17% below the brokers', because we do not assume a quick return to a 23%+ margin. FY26 (Mar-2026) is the last reported year; Q1FY27 (Jun-2026, reported 29/30-Jul-2026) is the last quarter known on 30-Sep-2026. One reported segment; revenue comes from the business-line build below (OHT tyres, third-party carbon black, on-highway tyres), checked against model revenue in BALKRISIND.ctx.js. EBITDA is on Screener's basis (foreign-exchange gains and losses inside expenses).
assumptions._revenueWhy: From the business-line build (sum checked in BALKRISIND.ctx.js). FY27E +22.6%: OHT tyres +19% (volume +11% to ~352,000 MT: Q1 +16% on a tariff-hit base, H2 against record FY26 quarters; realisation +7%: ~5% price increase in Q1, EUR realised ~Rs102 in Q1 and FY27 hedges at ~Rs107 vs Rs94-99 in FY26, partly offset by India rising to ~40% of volume), third-party carbon black +38% (capacity 265,000 to 360,000 MTPA, ~10% of Q1 revenue), on-highway Rs200 cr (seeding year). Check: Q1FY27 revenue of Rs3,455 cr is 26% of our FY27E, the same share Q1 had in FY25. FY28E-29E: OHT +11% / +10% (volume +8%/+7% as the 35,000 MTPA expansion and debottlenecking take capacity towards 425,000 MTPA, price/mix +3%), carbon black +12% / +10%, on-highway Rs600 cr / Rs1,100 cr (Anand Rathi: Rs600 cr in FY28E; company target Rs5,000 cr by FY30, which we do not assume). Street FY27E/FY28E revenue: ICICI Direct Rs13,407 / 15,826 cr (31-Jul-2026); Geojit Rs12,771 / 14,942 cr (pre-Q1).

build._note: Business-line build (Rs crore). FY26 consolidated revenue Rs10,823 cr split with management's statement that third-party carbon black was ~9% of the business in FY26 (Q4FY26 call); on-highway revenue was negligible in FY26 (launched Feb-Apr 2026). On-highway is entered in rupees, not as growth.

assumptions._marginWhy: Screener basis (FX gains and losses in expenses): FY24 24.1%, FY25 23.5%, FY26 21.3%, Q1FY27 21.5%. FY27E 20.5%: management expects raw material +5% in Q2-Q3 (~3% of sales), a ~2pp margin hit next quarter, offset over time by the ~5% Q1 price increase; freight ~5% of revenue and could rise; India (lower margin) ~40% of volume; employee cost +18% in Q1; on-highway start-up losses. Helped by smaller FX losses: FY27 hedges at ~Rs107/EUR against Rs94-99 realised in FY26 (FY26 FX swing: -Rs517 cr, standalone). FY28E 21.5%, FY29E 22.0%: the raw-material spike eases and hedges roll at higher rates, but third-party carbon black (industry-average margins, management) and on-highway (mid-single-digit margins, Anand Rathi) grow to ~15% of revenue. Management's 23-25% company-wide target is not assumed (bull case). Street FY28E: ICICI Direct 20.4% (standalone basis), Geojit 22.6%, Anand Rathi 23.2%.
assumptions._capexWhy: Rs6,800 cr plan to FY29 (incl. Rs2,000 cr approved May-2026): ~Rs3,800 cr spent by Jun-26, Rs3,000 cr left; Q1FY27 ~Rs1,000 cr and Rs1,500-2,000 cr more in FY27 (Q1 call, 30-Jul-2026): FY27E Rs2,800 cr. FY28-29E: the remaining ~Rs1,000-1,500 cr plus ~Rs200 cr a year of maintenance (Q4FY26 call). Cash capex was Rs3,003 cr in FY26 and Rs1,483 cr in FY25 (Screener).
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation Rs775 cr = 6.5% of average gross block (Rs11,903 cr, Screener; Rs11,278 cr at Mar-25, Rs12,527 cr at Mar-26). Q1FY27 Rs206 cr, rising ~3-4% a quarter as carbon black phase 2 and the CV radial line are capitalised. The engine depreciates new capex at once and holds CWIP (Rs2,472 cr at Mar-26) flat, so we use 6.3%: ~Rs880 cr in FY27E.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: BKT has net debt (Rs922 cr at Mar-26 on Screener's consolidated basis: debt Rs4,111 cr vs investments Rs3,124 cr and cash Rs65 cr; Rs1,725 cr standalone at Jun-26), so the engine's yield on net treasury would be zero. All treasury income is built in otherIncome below and all interest in interest.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Built from AR FY26 note 30. Treasury book at Mar-26: investments Rs3,124 cr + cash Rs65 cr, of which Rs637 cr is strategic equity (NSE stake Rs593 cr, start-ups) that earns only dividends; the interest-bearing and mark-to-market part (debt funds, Bharat Bond ETFs, AIFs, bonds) was ~Rs2,550 cr and earned Rs217 cr in FY26 (interest Rs47 cr, distributions Rs39 cr, realised and MTM gains Rs131 cr) = ~8.1% of the average book, flattered by falling rates. We use 7% on a book run down to ~Rs2,300 cr to fund capex (FY27E) and rebuilt to ~Rs2,600 cr (FY29E), plus dividends ~Rs18 cr (FY26 Rs17 cr) and other income ~Rs16 cr. FY27E Rs235 cr = Q1 actual Rs100 cr (incl. FX and MTM items) + ~Rs45 cr a quarter. FY26 Rs252 cr, TTM to Jun-26 Rs244 cr; FY25 Rs539 cr included a Rs267 cr FX gain that does not recur in our model.
assumptions._interestLabel: Interest cost (packing credit and other working-capital loans, NCDs, term loans)
assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 Rs134 cr on average debt of ~Rs3,690 cr (3.6%: mostly low-cost foreign-currency export credit; NCDs at 7.20-7.55%); Q1FY27 Rs37 cr. Debt rose to Rs4,690 cr (standalone) at Jun-26 and we expect ~Rs5,200 cr at Mar-27 as FY27 capex (Rs2,800 cr) exceeds operating cash; ~3.8% on ~Rs4,650 cr average = Rs175 cr. FY28E Rs185 cr (NCDs a larger share), FY29E Rs165 cr as free cash flow repays debt.
assumptions._payoutWhy: Rs16 a share in FY25 and FY26 (Rs4 a quarter) = 25% of FY26 EPS, 19% of FY25; first interim of Rs4 for FY27. 22% of our EPS is ~Rs16-21 a share.

dcf._betaWhy: Export-led (~64% of revenue), farm-cycle and currency-exposed, now with modest net debt (~2-4% of market value): beta 1.0, Ke 12.5%. Debt is small, so the cost of equity is the discount rate.
dcf._tgWhy: Global OHT volumes grow ~3% a year (Smithers via AR FY26: 52.5 mn to 57 mn units, 2026-29) and India OHT ~5.5%; BKT adds share gains and price. 5.5% nominal terminal growth (house range 5-6%).
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~13% to 8% over 12 years: share gains in a ~3% market, India and on-highway growth.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: EBITDA margin held at 22%: below the FY16-25 OHT-only history (mostly 24-26%) because carbon black and on-highway tyres earn less.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capital-hungry: capex fades to 7% of revenue (FY17-26 cash capex averaged ~16.5% of revenue in a build-out decade; 5-12% in the lighter years FY17, FY18 and FY24); depreciation 6% of revenue (FY26 7.2%).

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Europe and the US recover together (US duty stays ~10%, tariff refunds received), price increases stick as raw materials ease, the EUR stays near ₹107-110, and management's 23-25% margin target is met by FY29E even as on-highway scales.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: A hot, dry European season and weak farm incomes stall agricultural demand; crude-linked raw materials and freight keep rising with the Middle East conflict; the rupee strengthens against the hedge book; on-highway losses run longer, so the margin stays near 18-19%.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: How the street values BKT: P/E on one-year-forward EPS (MOSL 22x, ICICI Direct 27x, Anand Rathi 28x, Geojit 26x, all FY28E). Multiple derived in BALKRISIND.ctx.js and written by BALKRISIND.val.js.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Values the operating business; net debt at the target date is deducted.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 12-year FCFF, Ke 12.5%, terminal growth 5.5%, less net debt.
